name: ARMOR-WATCH
role: Minimal watch client: alarm notices and alarm confirmation
deployment_target: Wear OS 3+ watch paired with the phone
build: python tools/watch_contract.py && python -m unittest discover -s tests && ./gradlew test
notes: The watch shows the alarms and notices the phone chooses to send and lets the person confirm an alarm with one tap; it keeps nothing on the watch and holds no session of ARMOR-SERVER. Today the repository holds the message contract (docs/watch_alert_contract.json, checked in Python), the Kotlin core that reads and checks every message, keeps the alerts in memory and runs the conversation of the watch end against a simulated phone (tested on a computer with Gradle), the Wear OS app (wear/: a Compose for Wear OS screen and the Data Layer service, built only with -ParmorWear, compiled and unit-tested in GitHub Actions) and the protocol notes. The sending side is in ARMOR-ANDROID-CONTROL (off by default); an iPhone does not pair with a Wear OS watch, so there is no counterpart in ARMOR-IOS-CONTROL. Nothing has run on a real watch or an emulator.
